claims.statement: Hamsa is an aquatic bird in ancient Sanskrit texts serving as a spiritual symbol in India and Southeast Asia.
claims.statement_id: Hamsa adalah burung air dalam teks Sanskerta kuno yang menjadi simbol rohani budaya India dan Asia Tenggara.
claims.quote: is an aquatic migratory bird, referred to in ancient Sanskrit texts ... Its image is used in Indian and Southeast Asian culture as a spiritual symbol and a decorative element.

claims.statement: Scholars interpret its referent as goose, swan, or flamingo.
claims.statement_id: Para sarjana menafsirkan burung acuannya sebagai angsa, swan, atau flamingo.
claims.quote: various scholars have interpreted as being based on the goose, the swan, or even the flamingo.

claims.statement: It is associated with a mythical ability to separate milk from mixed milk and water.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikaitkan dengan kemampuan mitos memisahkan susu dari campuran susu dan air.
claims.quote: the bird attributed with the mythical ability to extract milk from a mixture of milk and water or good from evil.

claims.statement: In iconography it is the vehicle of Brahma, Gayatri, Saraswati, and Vishvakarma.

claims.statement: In Indian philosophical literature hamsa symbolizes the individual soul or universal spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sastra filsafat India, hamsa melambangkan jiwa individu atau roh universal.

claims.statement: The NHB interprets the hintha bird on a Burmese offering vessel as hamsa, Brahma's mount.

claims.statement: The legend recounts Kanthaka dying of a broken heart after parting from Siddhartha.

claims.statement: He pulls the chariot when Channa accompanies Siddhartha to the four sights prompting renunciation.

claims.statement: He carries Siddhartha out of the palace toward a forest by the Anoma river.

claims.statement_id: Manohara adalah kinnari, perempuan-burung, tokoh utama kisah Jataka.
claims.quote: is the kinnari (half-woman, half-bird) heroine of one of the Jataka tales.

claims.quote: Manoharā (Pali: "captivating", "heart-stealing") or Manoharī is the kinnari (half-woman, half-bird) heroine of one of the Jataka tales. Typically referred to as Manohara and Prince Sudhana, the legend appears in the Paññāsa Jātaka, Divyavadana and is documented by stone reliefs at Borobodur.

claims.statement: She is the youngest of the Kinnara king's seven daughters living on Kailash.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan putri termuda dari tujuh putri raja Kinnara yang tinggal di Kailash.
claims.quote: Manohara, the youngest of seven daughters of the Kimnara king, lives on Mount Kailash. One day, she travels to the human realm. She is caught by a hunter (using a magic noose in some versions) who gives her to Prince Sudhana. Son of King Adityavamsa and Queen Chandradevi, Sudhana is a renowned archer and heir to the Panchala kingdom.

claims.statement: A hunter captures her and gives her to Sudhana, who later marries her.
claims.statement_id: Seorang pemburu menangkapnya dan memberikannya kepada Sudhana, yang kemudian menikahinya.
claims.quote: She is caught by a hunter (using a magic noose in some versions) who gives her to Prince Sudhana. ... The prince falls in love with Manohara, and they get married.

claims.statement: When accused of bringing misfortune and threatened with death she flies home, leaving a ring and directions for Sudhana.
claims.statement_id: Ketika dituduh membawa kesialan dan diancam mati, ia terbang pulang dan meninggalkan cincin serta petunjuk bagi Sudhana.
claims.quote: Later, when the prince is away in battle, Manohara is accused by the royal counselor of bringing bad luck to the city and is threatened with death. claims.statement: Sarama or Devashuni is the gods' female dog in Hindu mythology.
claims.statement_id: Sarama atau Devashuni adalah anjing betina para dewa dalam mitologi Hindu.
claims.quote: is a female dog of the gods in Hindu mythology.

claims.statement: In the Rigveda she helps Indra recover divine cows stolen by the Panis.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Rigveda ia membantu Indra menemukan sapi ilahi yang dicuri para Pani.
claims.quote: Sarama (Sanskrit: सरमा, Saramā) or Devashuni (Sanskrit: देव-शुनी, Devaśunī) is a female dog of the gods in Hindu mythology. She first appears in one of Hinduism's earliest texts, the Rig Veda, in which she helps the king of the gods Indra to recover divine cows stolen by the Panis asuras. This legend is alluded to in many later texts, and Sarama is often associated with Indra.

claims.statement: Early Rigvedic texts do not directly call her a dog; later Vedic interpretations do.
claims.statement_id: Teks Rigveda awal tidak langsung menyebutnya anjing; tafsir Weda belakangan menyebutnya demikian.
claims.quote: Early Rig Vedic works do not directly call Sarama a "dog," but her actions, behavior, and onomatopoeia in R.V. 10.108 provide a vivid description of a dog's behavior, and dogs in the Rig Veda are often given the name Sarameya—daughters of Sarama. In addition later Vedic mythologies and interpretations also directly call Sarama as a dog.

claims.statement: She is called mother of Yama's two four eyed brindled dogs.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut ibu dua anjing Yama bermata empat dan berbulu belang.
claims.quote: the mother of all dogs, in particular of the two four-eyed brindle dogs of the god Yama,

claims.statement: The epithet Devashuni means divine bitch or bitch of the gods.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan Devashuni berarti anjing betina ilahi atau anjing betina para dewa.
claims.quote: Sarama's other name Deva-shuni means "divine bitch" or "bitch of the gods".

      effect of the curse.

claims.statement: Shakchunni is a female ghost in Bengali folklore, the spirit of a Hindu woman dying before her husband.
claims.statement_id: Shakchunni adalah hantu perempuan dalam cerita rakyat Bengali, roh perempuan Hindu yang mati sebelum suaminya.
claims.quote: Shakchunni ... is a female ghost in Bengali folklore, ... The term refers to the spirit of a married Hindu woman who died while still married (i.e., before her husband).

claims.statement: She retains shankha conch bangles and sindoor vermilion, symbols of marriage.
claims.statement_id: Ia mempertahankan gelang kerang shankha dan vermilion sindoor, lambang perkawinan.
claims.quote: The word Shakchunni is derived from the Sanskrit term Shankhachurni. In Bengali Hindu tradition, married women traditionally wear conch-shell bangles (shankha) and vermilion (sindoor) as symbols of marriage. The Shakchunni is believed to retain these symbols even after death, reflecting her continued attachment to married life.

claims.statement: She is said to possess married women to relive household life.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikisahkan merasuki perempuan menikah untuk mengalami lagi kehidupan rumah tangga.
claims.quote: According to folklore, a Shakchunni is the spirit of a married woman whose desires and attachments to domestic life remain unfulfilled at the time of her death. She is often portrayed as longing for marital happiness and household life, and is said to possess or influence married women, especially those from affluent households, in order to relive such experiences.

claims.statement: In many tales an ojha eventually expels or defeats the spirit.
claims.statement_id: Dalam banyak kisah, ojha akhirnya mengusir atau mengalahkan roh ini.
claims.quote: Stories featuring Shakchunni appear in traditional Bengali folktales, including those found in collections such as Thakurmar Jhuli. In many narratives, an exorcist (ojha) ultimately defeats or expels her spirit.

claims.statement: Lavana or Lavanasura is an asura killed by Shatrughna in the Ramayana.
claims.statement_id: Lavana atau Lavanasura adalah asura yang dibunuh Shatrughna dalam Ramayana.
claims.quote: Lavana (Sanskrit: लवणासुर, romanized: Lavaṇāsura) is an asura in Hinduism. He is slain by Shatrughna, the youngest brother of Rama, in the Hindu epic Ramayana.

claims.statement: He is Madhu and Kumbhini's son.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan putra Madhu dan Kumbhini.
claims.quote: Lavana was the son of an asura king named Madhu and his wife, Kumbhini.

claims.statement: He troubles sages and destroys rituals so they ask Rama for protection.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengganggu para resi dan menghancurkan ritual sehingga mereka meminta perlindungan Rama.
claims.quote: During Rama's reign, while peace prevailed in most places, Lavanasura continued to torment the innocent and destroy many sacrifices of sages and terrify them in many ways. Many kings were defeated by him and they were all afraid. Therefore, one day, the sages headed by sage Chyavana (a descendant of sage Bhrigu), came all the way from Madhupuri to Rama with a plea to protect them.

claims.statement: Madhu passes down his trident to Lavana.
claims.statement_id: Madhu mewariskan trisulanya kepada Lavana.
claims.quote: Madhu handed everything over to his son including his trident

claims.statement: Rama warns Shatrughna to fight him while he is without the invincible trident.
claims.statement_id: Rama memperingatkan Shatrughna untuk melawannya saat ia tidak memegang trisula yang tak terkalahkan.
claims.quote: Rama warned his brother to find a way to fight with Lavana without his holding the invincible trident.

claims.statement: During the fight Lavana uproots trees and throws them at Shatrughna.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pertarungan, Lavana mencabut pohon dan melemparkannya ke Shatrughna.
claims.quote: Lavana uprooted many trees and threw them on Shatrughna, and a great battle ensued.

claims.statement: According to this retelling, the rakshasa Madhu received a boon from Shiva in the form of an invincible spear (shula) that could reduce enemies to ashes.
claims.statement_id: Menurut penuturan ini, raksasa Madhu menerima anugerah dari Shiva berupa tombak (shula) yang tak terkalahkan; tombak itu mampu menghanguskan musuh menjadi abu.
claims.quote: In the past, a rākṣasa named Madhu received a boon from Śiva, because of which he got an invincible śūla – spear. The spear was endowed with the ability to reduce enemies to ashes.

claims.statement: Madhu passed away after giving the spear to his ruthless son Lavana. Lavanasura is described as tormenting the worlds with his vile nature and the special power of the spear.
claims.statement_id: Madhu wafat setelah menyerahkan tombak itu kepada putranya yang kejam, Lavana. Lavanasura digambarkan menyiksa dunia dengan sifat buruknya dan kekuatan khusus tombak itu.
claims.quote: Madhu passed away bestowing the spear to his ruthless son Lavaṇa. Now, this Lavaṇāsura torments the worlds with his vile nature and the special power of the spear.

claims.statement: Rama gave Shatrughna a powerful arrow created by Vishnu and sent him with a large army to vanquish Lavanasura.
claims.statement_id: Rama menghadiahkan kepada Shatrughna sebuah panah kuat ciptaan Wisnu dan mengirimnya bersama pasukan besar untuk menaklukkan Lavanasura.
claims.quote: Rāma gifted Śatrughna a powerful arrow created by Viṣṇu and sent him with a large army to vanquish Lavaṇāsura.

claims.statement: Shatrughna arrived at a sage's hermitage on the banks of the River Yamuna and slew Lavanasura with the arrow Rama had given him.
claims.statement_id: Shatrughna tiba di pertapaan seorang resi di tepi Sungai Yamuna, lalu membunuh Lavanasura dengan panah pemberian Rama.
claims.quote: The next morning, Śatrughna took leave of Sage Vālmīki and arrived at the āśrama of Sage Cyavana on the banks of River Yamunā. He slew Lavaṇāsura using the arrow Rāma had gifted him.

claims.statement: It is stated that Mandhata once fought Lavanasura but had to accept defeat before the god-given spear that Lavanasura possessed.
claims.statement_id: Disebutkan bahwa Mandhata pernah melawan Lavanasura tetapi harus mengaku kalah menghadapi tombak pemberian dewa yang dimiliki Lavanasura.
claims.quote: Māndhātā had to fight once against Lavaṇāsura but had to accept defeat before the god-given spear which Lavaṇāsura possessed. (Uttara Rāmāyaṇa).

claims.statement: In this source it is Rama, at the request of the munis of the Yamuna plain, who killed Lavanasura, son of Madhu, in the great city called Durga in the middle of the Madhu forest.
claims.statement_id: Dalam sumber ini, Rama (atas permintaan para muni di dataran Yamuna) yang membunuh Lavanasura, putra Madhu, di kota besar bernama Durga di tengah hutan Madhu.
claims.quote: It was during this period that Rāma, as desired by the munis in the Yamunā plain, killed Lavaṇāsura, son of Madhu in the great city called Durga in the centre of the Madhu forest.

claims.statement: Pakhangba is a primordial dragon deity in Meitei mythology and Manipur's Sanamahism.
claims.statement_id: Pakhangba adalah dewa primordial berwujud naga dalam mitologi Meitei dan Sanamahism Manipur.
claims.quote: is a primordial deity, often represented in the form of a dragon, in Meitei mythology and Sanamahism, the indigenous religion of Manipur.

claims.statement: His figure appears in Manipur royal heraldry derived from mythical paphal illustrations.
claims.statement_id: Figurnya muncul dalam lambang kerajaan Manipur, berasal dari ilustrasi mitos paphal.
claims.quote: Pakhangba (Meitei: ꯄꯥꯈꯪꯕ, lit. 'the one who knows his father') is a primordial deity, often represented in the form of a dragon, in Meitei mythology and Sanamahism, the indigenous religion of Manipur. He is depicted in the heraldry of the Manipur kingdom, which originated in paphal (Meitei: ꯄꯥꯐꯜ), mythical illustrations of the deity.

claims.statement: His identity is often fused with the first Ningthouja ruler also named Pakhangba.
claims.statement_id: Identitasnya sering dipadukan dengan raja pertama Ningthouja yang juga bernama Pakhangba.
claims.quote: The identity of the deity is often fused with Nongda Lairen Pakhangba, the first ruler of the Ningthouja dynasty. The title Pakhangba was also used by other kings in the history of Manipur.

claims.statement: Following his mother's advice he circles his father's throne as equivalent to circling the universe and gains the throne.
claims.statement_id: Atas petunjuk ibunya, ia mengelilingi takhta ayahnya sebagai padanan mengelilingi alam semesta dan memperoleh takhta.
claims.quote: His mother Leimarel Sidabi, said that circling his father's throne is equivalent to the circling of the entire universe. So, he circled the throne, and his father was satisfied with Pakhangba's knowledge. ... and was enthroned.

claims.statement: He is depicted as a serpent with sangai deer antlers.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai ular dengan tanduk rusa sangai.
claims.quote: Pakhangba is depicted as a serpent with the antlers of a sangai, or brow-antlered deer,

claims.statement: N. Khelchandra Singh recounts a god king Pakhangba version moving as a dragon at night and called Sanahing Pakhangba.
claims.statement_id: N. Khelchandra Singh menuturkan versi raja-dewa Pakhangba yang bergerak sebagai naga pada malam hari dan dikenal sebagai Sanahing Pakhangba.
claims.quote: Because of his divine power to be able to move about at night as dragon he is also known as Sanahing Pakhangba.

claims.statement: The World Turtle is a motif of a giant turtle supporting or containing the world.
claims.statement_id: World Turtle adalah motif kura-kura raksasa yang menopang atau memuat dunia.
claims.quote: is a mytheme of a giant turtle (or tortoise) supporting or containing the world.

claims.statement: The motif occurs in Hindu, Chinese, and some Indigenous American traditions.
claims.statement_id: Motifnya ditemukan dalam tradisi Hindu, Tiongkok, dan sebagian masyarakat pribumi Amerika.
claims.quote: It occurs in Hinduism, Chinese mythology, and the mythologies of some of the indigenous peoples of the Americas.

claims.statement: In Hindu tradition the world turtle is known as Akupara or Chukwa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Hindu, kura-kura dunia dikenal sebagai Akupara atau Chukwa.
claims.quote: The World Turtle in Hinduism is known as Akūpāra (Sanskrit: अकूपार), or sometimes Chukwa.

claims.statement: The Chinese version tells of Nuwa using Ao's legs to support the sky after Gong Gong damages Mount Buzhou.
claims.statement_id: Versi Tiongkok menuturkan Nuwa memakai kaki kura-kura Ao untuk menopang langit setelah Gong Gong merusak Gunung Buzhou.
claims.quote: In the Chinese mythology, the creator goddess Nüwa cut the legs off the giant sea turtle Ao (simplified Chinese: 鳌; traditional Chinese: 鰲; pinyin: áo) and used them to prop up the sky after Gong Gong damaged Mount Buzhou, which had previously supported the heavens.

claims.statement: The Lenape Great Turtle story was recorded by Jasper Danckaerts in 1678–1680.
claims.statement_id: Kisah Great Turtle Lenape dicatat Jasper Danckaerts pada 1678–1680.
claims.quote: The Lenape creation story of the "Great Turtle" was first recorded between 1678 and 1680 by Jasper Danckaerts. The belief is shared by other indigenous peoples of the Northeastern Woodlands, most notably those of the Haudenosaunee confederacy, and the Anishinaabeg.

claims.statement: In Mackenzie's retelling movement of Kurma's limbs makes Shesha yawn and causes earthquakes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam penuturan Mackenzie, gerak anggota badan Kurma membuat Shesha menguap dan menimbulkan gempa.
claims.quote:
When the tortoise moves its limbs, Shesha is
roused to yawn; thus are earthquakes caused.

claims.statement: Akuma is an evil spirit in Japanese folklore also called ma.
claims.statement_id: Akuma adalah roh jahat dalam cerita rakyat Jepang yang juga disebut ma.
claims.quote: is an evil spirit in Japanese folklore, sometimes described in English-language sources as a devil or demon. ... An alternative name for the akuma is ma

claims.statement: Early uses of the word akuma are mainly found in Buddhist texts.
claims.statement_id: Pemakaian awal kata akuma terutama ditemukan dalam teks Buddha.
claims.quote: The earliest uses of the word akuma are mainly found in Buddhist texts,

claims.statement: The word also appears in literary works of the Heian period.
claims.statement_id: Kata itu juga muncul dalam karya sastra zaman Heian.
claims.quote: it also appears in literary works, especially those written during the Heian period

claims.statement: Akuma is depicted with a fiery head, flaming eyes, and a sword.
claims.statement_id: Akuma digambarkan berkepala berapi, bermata menyala, dan membawa pedang.
claims.quote: An akuma is typically depicted as an entity with a fiery head and flaming eyes, and carrying a sword.

claims.statement: Seeing one is believed to herald misfortune.
claims.statement_id: Melihatnya dipercaya menjadi pertanda kesialan.
claims.quote: It is said to be a harbinger of misfortune to those who see it.

claims.statement: It is said to possess people and cause natural disasters.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan merasuki orang dan menyebabkan bencana alam.
claims.quote: They are said to possess people and cause natural disasters.

claims.statement: An old Japanese–English dictionary lists Akuma as a synonym for a demon or evil spirit.
claims.statement_id: Kamus Jepang–Inggris lama mencantumkan Akuma sebagai sinonim iblis atau roh jahat.

claims.statement: The crocotta is a mythical dog-wolf placed in India or Aethiopia.
claims.statement_id: Crocotta adalah hewan mitos mirip anjing-serigala yang ditempatkan di India atau Aethiopia.
claims.quote: is a mythical dog-wolf of India or Aethiopia, linked to the hyena

claims.statement: It is said to be a deadly enemy of humans and dogs.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan menjadi musuh mematikan manusia dan anjing.
claims.quote: said to be a deadly enemy of men and dogs.

claims.statement: Strabo describes it as mixed offspring of a wolf and dog.
claims.statement_id: Strabo menggambarkannya sebagai keturunan campuran serigala dan anjing.
claims.quote: Strabo, who uses the word "crocuttas", describes the beast as the mixed progeny of a wolf and a dog (Geographica, XVI.4.16]).

claims.statement: Pliny describes it as a hybrid of hyena and lion.
claims.statement_id: Pliny menggambarkannya sebagai campuran hiena dan singa.
claims.quote: Pliny in his work Natural History (VIII.72 and 107) describes the crocotta as a hybrid between a hyena and lion:

claims.statement: Pliny's description gives its jaws an unbroken bone ridge as teeth without gums.
claims.statement_id: Deskripsi Pliny menyebut rahangnya memiliki satu punggung tulang sebagai gigi tanpa gusi.
claims.quote: It has an unbroken ridge of bone in each jaw, forming a continuous tooth without any gum.

claims.statement: Pliny's Natural History translation says the corocotta imitates human and cattle voices.
claims.statement_id: Terjemahan Natural History Pliny menyebut corocotta meniru suara manusia dan ternak.
claims.quote:
which has the same faculty of imitating the voices of
men and cattle.

claims.statement: Keshi is a Hindu horse demon killed by Krishna.
claims.statement_id: Keshi adalah iblis kuda Hindu yang dibunuh Krishna.
claims.quote: is a horse-demon, killed by Krishna, an Avatara of Vishnu.

claims.statement: Kamsa sends him to attack Krishna.
claims.statement_id: Kamsa mengirimnya untuk menyerang Krishna.
claims.quote: The demon was dispatched by Krishna's evil uncle Kamsa

claims.statement: His death story appears in the Bhagavata Purana, Vishnu Purana, and Harivamsa.
claims.statement_id: Kisah kematiannya terdapat dalam Bhagavata Purana, Vishnu Purana, dan Harivamsa.
claims.quote: The tale of the slaying of Keshi is told in the Hindu scriptures of Bhagavata Purana, Vishnu Purana and Harivamsa. Krishna is often praised as Keshava - the slayer of Keshi - in scriptures.

claims.statement: He assumes a huge horse form whose neighing frightens people.
claims.statement_id: Ia mengambil wujud kuda raksasa yang ringkikannya menakutkan orang.
claims.quote: Keshi assumes the form of a huge horse, ... His neighing terrifies the people.

claims.statement: Krishna seizes his two legs and throws him far away.
claims.statement_id: Krishna menangkap kedua kakinya dan melemparkannya jauh.
claims.quote: Krishna catches hold of Keshi's two legs and tosses him to a great distance.

claims.statement: In the Bhagavata Purana translation Krishna's expanding arm blocks Keshi's breathing until he dies.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Bhagavata Purana, lengan Krishna membesar dan menghalangi napas Keshi hingga ia mati.
claims.quote: As Lord Kṛṣṇa’s expanding arm completely blocked Keśī’s breathing, ... The demon then passed stool and fell on the ground, dead.

claims.statement: Mahoraga are a group of reptilian deities in Hindu, Buddhist, and Jain traditions.
claims.statement_id: Mahoraga adalah kelompok dewa reptil dalam tradisi Hindu, Buddha, dan Jain.
claims.quote: are a race of deities in Hinduism, Buddhism, and Jainism. ... a race of primordial reptilian beings

claims.statement: Depictions can have reptilian bodies from the waist down.
claims.statement_id: Penggambarannya dapat memiliki tubuh reptil dari pinggang ke bawah.
claims.quote: Like the nāga, they are often depicted as anthropomorphic beings with reptilian bodies from the waist down.

claims.statement: They belong to eight classes of deities protecting the Dharma.
claims.statement_id: Mereka termasuk delapan golongan dewa pelindung Dharma.
claims.quote: The Mahoraga are one of the eight classes of deities (aṣṭasenā) that are said to protect the Dharma.

claims.statement: They are described as huge underground serpents rotating the earth and sometimes causing earthquakes.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikisahkan sebagai ular besar di bawah tanah yang memutar bumi dan kadang menyebabkan gempa.
claims.quote: They are described as huge subterranean serpents who lie on their sides and rotate the earth, which occasionally causes earthquakes.

claims.statement: They are also associated with instrumental music.
claims.statement_id: Mereka juga dikaitkan dengan musik instrumental.
claims.quote: Like the kinnara, the Mahoraga are also associated with instrumental music. They are understood as being associated with large serpents such as pythons, while the nāgas are more closely related to the cobra.

claims.statement: In Soothill's Lotus Sutra translation mahoragas join other beings in honoring the Buddha.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan Lotus Sutra Soothill, mahoraga hadir bersama makhluk lain dan menghormati Buddha.
claims.quote:
Then the monks and nuns, male and female disciples, gods, nagas,
yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and others,
all the great assembly of beings, human and not human, rejoice greatly,
each doffing his robe and offering it in homage to the Buddha.

claims.statement: The name is also pronounced Maha-Uraga, which Wikipedia renders as "Greater Reptilians".
claims.statement_id: Nama itu juga diucapkan Maha-Uraga, yang diterjemahkan Wikipedia sebagai "Greater Reptilians" (reptil yang lebih besar).
claims.quote: also pronounced as Maha-Uraga ("Greater Reptilians"),

claims.statement: The Mahoraga are the exalted ones among the Uragas, a race of primordial reptilian beings who are cousins to the nāga.
claims.statement_id: Mahoraga adalah yang terluhur di antara para Uraga, ras makhluk reptil purba yang bersepupu dengan naga.
claims.quote: They are the exalted ones among the Uragas, a race of primordial reptilian beings who are cousins to the nāga.

claims.statement: Their appearance can differ by artistic tradition, sometimes with serpent skin and humanoid bodies, or a serpent head on the body of a muscular divine human.
claims.statement_id: Penampilan mereka dapat berbeda menurut tradisi seni: kadang berkulit ular dengan tubuh humanoid, atau berkepala ular dengan tubuh manusia ilahi yang berotot.
claims.quote: However, their appearance can differ depending on artistic tradition, sometimes having serpent skin with humanoid bodies, or having a serpent head with the body of a muscular divine human.

claims.statement: An illustration from an 1866 Japanese book shows a mahoraga, in this scene an incarnation of Bodhisattva Kannon, giving a sermon to folk.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah ilustrasi dari buku Jepang tahun 1866 menampilkan mahoraga, dalam adegan itu penjelmaan Bodhisattva Kannon, yang berkhotbah kepada orang-orang.
claims.quote: An illustration from an 1866 Japanese book. Mahoraga, who is an incarnation of Bodhisattva Kannon in this scene, gives a sermon to folks.

claims.statement: The Buddhism glossary on Wisdom Library records the mahoraga as a deity with the head of a snake who protects Buddhists.
claims.statement_id: Glosarium Buddhisme di Wisdom Library mencatat mahoraga sebagai dewa berkepala ular yang melindungi umat Buddha.
claims.quote: Mahoraga:—A deity with the head of a snake who protects Buddhists.

claims.statement: In Jainism, according to Wisdom Library, the mahoragas are a group of deities of the vyantara class, eight groups of deities that wander about the three worlds (adhaloka, madhyaloka and ūrdhvaloka).
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Jain, menurut Wisdom Library, mahoraga adalah kelompok dewa dari golongan vyantara, delapan kelompok dewa yang mengembara di tiga dunia (adhaloka, madhyaloka, dan ūrdhvaloka).
claims.quote: The mahoragas are a group of deities categorised as belonging to the vyantara class of Gods (devas). The vyantaras represent a class of Gods (devas) comprising eight groups of deities that wander about the three worlds (adhaloka, madhyaloka and ūrdhvaloka).

claims.statement: According to a Jain source quoted on Wisdom Library, the Mahoragas have a dark complexion and the Naga-tree is their Caitya-tree.
claims.statement_id: Menurut sumber Jain yang dikutip Wisdom Library, para mahoraga berkulit gelap dan pohon Naga adalah pohon Caitya mereka.
claims.quote: The Mahoragas have dark complexion. The Nāga-tree is their Caitya-tree.

claims.statement: Mahoraga (महोरग) refers to the "great serpent" class of "peripatetic celestial beings" (vyantara), a category of devas, according to the 2nd-century Tattvarthasutra.
claims.statement_id: Mahoraga (महोरग) merujuk pada golongan "ular besar" dari "makhluk langit pengembara" (vyantara), kategori dewa, menurut Tattvarthasutra abad ke-2.
claims.quote: Mahoraga (महोरग) refers to the “great serpent” class of “peripatetic celestial beings” (vyantara), itself a category of devas (celestial beings), according to the 2nd-century Tattvārthasūtra 4.10.

claims.statement: In Tibetan Buddhism, according to Wisdom Library, mahoraga also refers to a group of deities summoned by the Yamantaka mantra and mentioned as attending the teachings in the 6th-century Manjusrimulakalpa.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Buddhisme Tibet, menurut Wisdom Library, mahoraga juga merujuk pada kelompok dewa yang dipanggil mantra Yamantaka dan disebut hadir pada ajaran dalam Manjusrimulakalpa abad ke-6.
claims.quote: Mahoraga (महोरग) also refers to a group of deities summoned by the Yamāntaka-mantra and mentioned as attending the teachings in the 6th century Mañjuśrīmūlakalpa.

claims.statement: Soothill's Lotus Sutra translation contains a question to King of Healing asking whether he sees in the assembly gods, dragon-kings, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, and human and non-human beings.
claims.statement_id: Lotus Sutra terjemahan Soothill memuat pertanyaan kepada Raja Penyembuhan apakah ia melihat di majelis itu para dewa, raja naga, yaksha, gandharva, asura, garuda, kinnara, mahoraga, makhluk manusia dan bukan manusia.
claims.quote: King of Healing! Do you see in this assembly innumerable gods, dragon-kings, yakshas, gandharvas, asuras, garudas, kinnaras, mahoragas, human and non-human beings, as well as monks, nuns, male and female lay devotees

claims.statement: Manibhadra is a major yaksha and a popular deity in ancient India.
claims.statement_id: Manibhadra adalah salah satu yaksha utama dan dewa populer di India kuno.
claims.quote: Maṇibhadra (Sanskrit: 'as excellent as a jewel') is one of the major yakshas. He was a popular deity in ancient India.

claims.statement: The name Manibhadra is explained as excellent as a jewel.
claims.statement_id: Nama Manibhadra diterangkan berarti seunggul permata.
claims.quote: (Sanskrit: 'as excellent as a jewel') is one of the major yakshas.

claims.statement: In Buddhist accounts he is said to dwell at Manimalachaitya in Magadha.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kisah Buddha, ia dikatakan menghuni Manimalachaitya di Magadha.
claims.quote: In Samyukta Nikaya,  Manibhadra is said to reside in the Manimala chaitya  in Magadha. Yaksha Manibhadra is invoked in The Exalted Manibhadra’s Dhārani.

claims.statement: Jain literature calls him leader of northern yakshas while Purnabhadra leads the south.
claims.statement_id: Sastra Jain menyebutnya pemimpin yaksha utara, sementara Purnabhadra memimpin selatan.
claims.quote: In Sūryaprajñapti, a Manibhadra chairya in Mithila is mentioned. Yakshas are referred to in the Harivamsa Purana (783 A.D.) of Jinasena made the beginning of this concept. Among them, Manibhadra and Purnabadra yakshas and Bahuputrika yakshini have been the most popular.

claims.statement: Among Gujarat Jains he is worshipped with Airavata, a multi tusked elephant mount.
claims.statement_id: Di kalangan Jain Gujarat ia dipuja dengan tunggangan Airavata, gajah bergading banyak.
claims.quote: Manibhadra Yaksha (or Vira) is a popular demigod among the Jains in Gujarat. ... he is shown with a multi-tusked elephant Airavata.

claims.statement: Mackenzie records Manibhadra being worshipped by travelers and resembling Kuvera, the god of wealth.
claims.statement_id: Mackenzie mencatat Manibhadra dipuja oleh para pelancong dan menyerupai dewa kekayaan Kuvera.
claims.quote:
Manibhadra, the demi-god, was worshipped by travellers, and resembles Kuvera,
god of wealth.

claims.statement: Matarisvan is a name of Agni or a divine being closely associated with Agni in the Rigveda.
claims.statement_id: Matarisvan adalah nama Agni atau makhluk ilahi yang dekat dengan Agni dalam Rigveda.
claims.quote: in the Rigveda is a name of Agni ... or of a divine being closely associated with Agni,

claims.statement: His name is interpreted as growing in the mother.
claims.statement_id: Namanya ditafsirkan berarti tumbuh dalam ibu.
claims.quote: ("growing in the mother", from the locative of "mother", mātari, and a root śvi "to grow, swell")

claims.statement: A messenger for Vivasvat, he delivers concealed fire to the Bhrigu lineage.
claims.statement_id: Ia disebut utusan Vivasvat yang membawa api tersembunyi kepada para Bhrigu.
claims.quote: a messenger of Vivasvat, bringing the hidden fire to the Bhrigus.

claims.statement: The commentator Sayana equates him with the wind deity Vayu when discussing RV 1.93.6.
claims.statement_id: Sayana menyamakannya dengan Vayu, angin, dalam tafsir RV 1.93.6.
claims.quote: Sayana identifies him with Vayu, the wind, in RV 1.93.6.

claims.statement: Later texts, including the Atharvaveda, also use the term for moving air and breezes.
claims.statement_id: Dalam Atharvaveda dan kemudian, kata itu juga bermakna udara, angin, atau embusan.
claims.quote: In the Atharvaveda and later, the word also has the meaning of "air, wind, breeze".

claims.statement: In the hymn excerpt presented by Mackenzie Matarisvan brings Agni as a gift to Bhrigu.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan himne yang disajikan Mackenzie, Matarisvan membawa Agni sebagai hadiah kepada Bhrigu.
claims.quote:
brought Agni to Bhrigu
as a gift, precious like wealth

claims.statement: Navagunjara is a Hindu legendary creature composed of nine animals.
claims.statement_id: Navagunjara adalah makhluk legenda Hindu gabungan sembilan hewan.
claims.quote: Navaguñjara (Sanskrit: नवगुञ्जर), or Nabaguñjara (Odia: ନବଗୁଞ୍ଜର) is a magical legendary creature composed of nine different animals in Hinduism.

claims.statement: He is a common motif in Odisha's Pattachitra art.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjadi motif umum seni Pattachitra Odisha.
claims.quote: The animal is a common motif in the Pattachitra style of painting, of the Eastern Indian state of Odisha. It is considered an astral form of the god Vishnu, or of Krishna, who is considered an avatar of Lord Vishnu.

claims.statement: He is considered a form of Vishnu or Krishna and a variant of Vishvarupa.
claims.statement_id: Ia dianggap wujud Vishnu atau Krishna dan varian Vishvarupa.
claims.quote: It is considered an astral form of the god Vishnu, or of Krishna, ... It is considered a variant of the Vishvarupa

claims.statement: His story is told in Sarala Dasa's Odia Mahabharata.
claims.statement_id: Kisahnya dituturkan dalam Mahabharata Odia karya Sarala Dasa.
claims.quote: The version of the Hindu epic Mahabharata, written by the Odia poet Sarala Dasa, narrates the legend of Navagunjara;

claims.statement: He has a rooster's head, elephant, tiger, and deer or horse legs, and a human arm carrying a lotus or wheel.
claims.statement_id: Ia berkepala ayam jantan, dengan kaki gajah, harimau, dan rusa atau kuda serta lengan manusia membawa teratai atau roda.
claims.quote: Navagunjara has the head of a rooster, and stands on three feet, those of an elephant, tiger and deer or horse; the fourth limb is a raised human arm carrying a lotus or a wheel.

claims.statement: Arjuna first aims to shoot him, then recognizes Vishnu's manifestation and bows.
claims.statement_id: Arjuna mula-mula hendak menembaknya, kemudian mengenali manifestasi Vishnu dan menunduk.
claims.quote: Initially, Arjuna was terrified as well as mesmerized by the strange creature and raises his bow to shoot it. Finally, Arjuna realizes that Navagunjara is a manifestation of Vishnu and drops his weapons, bowing before Navagunjara.

claims.statement: Bernard Cesarone explains the nava-gunjara theme as Vishnu or Krishna in a composite of nine animals.
claims.statement_id: Bernard Cesarone menjelaskan tema nava-gunjara sebagai Vishnu atau Krishna dalam gabungan sembilan hewan.
claims.quote:
Vishnu or Krishna is shown as a composite creature of 
        nine different animals

claims.statement: An Acheri is a girl spirit in Kumaon folklore in the southern Himalayas.
claims.statement_id: Acheri adalah roh gadis dalam cerita rakyat wilayah Kumaon di Himalaya selatan.
claims.quote: An Acheri is a spirit of a young girl in the folklore of the southern Himalayas, specifically regions around Kumaon.

claims.statement: Some accounts associate her with girls or women dying violently.
claims.statement_id: Sejumlah kisah menghubungkannya dengan gadis atau perempuan yang mati secara keras.
claims.quote: An Acheri is a spirit of a young girl (and in many accounts women) who died a violent death. Acheris are also referred to as "hill fairies", "Bhúts", and "hill godlings".

claims.statement: She dwells in the mountains by day and descends to revel at dusk.

claims.quote: is a class of supernatural beings in Hindu mythology. ... they are often described as attendants of Kubera, the keeper of wealth, and protect his hidden treasures.

claims.statement: Their name means hidden ones and is associated with dwelling in mountain caves.
claims.statement_id: Nama mereka berarti yang tersembunyi, dikaitkan dengan tempat tinggal di gua gunung.
claims.quote: Guhyaka(s) (गुह्यक, literally "hidden ones") ... Guhyakas are believed to live in mountain caves; thus their name, "hidden ones".

claims.statement: He is depicted as a giant with a frightening face and protruding fangs in Newar tales.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan sebagai raksasa berwajah menakutkan dan bertaring menonjol dalam cerita Newar.
claims.quote: The story of Gurumapa is one of the most well known folk tales in Newar society. He is depicted as a giant with a terrifying face and protruding fangs.

claims.statement: The report permits Gurumapa to devour children's dead bodies under a bargain.
claims.statement_id: Versi liputan menyebut Gurumapa mendapat izin memakan mayat anak sebagai bagian kesepakatan.
claims.quote: Gurumapa could devour the dead bodies of children.

claims.statement: In the reported version he is banished to Tundikhel.
claims.statement_id: Versi liputan menyebut raksasa itu dibuang ke Tundikhel.
claims.quote: he banished the demon to Tundikhel

claims.statement: Residents persuade him to move to Tundikhel with annual offerings of boiled rice and buffalo meat.
claims.statement_id: Warga membujuknya pindah ke Tundikhel dengan janji persembahan tahunan nasi rebus dan daging kerbau.
claims.quote: They promised to provide him an annual feast of boiled rice and buffalo meat if he agreed to live on the field of Tinkhya (Tundikhel).

claims.statement: Nepali Times records four copper plates narrating the Gurumapa legend.
claims.statement_id: Nepali Times mencatat empat lempeng tembaga menuturkan legenda Gurumapa.
claims.quote: four copper plates ... the legend of Gurumapa

claims.statement: Hydaspes is a river god in Greek mythology associated with the Jhelum.
claims.statement_id: Hydaspes adalah dewa sungai dalam mitologi Yunani yang dikaitkan dengan Jhelum.
claims.quote: was a river god of Pentapotamia ... It is the modern day Jhelum River

claims.statement: He is the son of Thaumas and Elektra, an Oceanid.
claims.statement_id: Ia merupakan putra Thaumas dan Elektra, seorang Oceanid.
claims.quote: Hydaspes was a Titan-descended god, the son of the sea-god Thaumas and the cloud-goddess Elektra, an Oceanid.

claims.statement: Iris is his sister.
claims.statement_id: Iris adalah saudara perempuannya.
claims.quote: He was the brother of Iris, the messenger goddess of the rainbow.

claims.statement: With Astris, Helios's daughter, he fathers Deriades.
claims.statement_id: Bersama Astris, putri Helios, ia menjadi ayah Deriades.
claims.quote: By the Heliad Astris, the daughter of Helios and the Oceanid Ceto, Hydaspes fathered Deriades the king of Pentapotamia (Punjab).

claims.statement: Nonnus's Dionysiaca recounts his support for the inhabitants in their war against Dionysos.
claims.statement_id: Dionysiaca Nonnus menuturkan dukungannya bagi penduduk dalam perang melawan Dionysos.
claims.quote: The poet Nonnus in his Dionysiaca mentioned Hydaspes supported the natives in their war against the invading armies of the god Dionysos.

claims.statement: In the Nonnus excerpt Hydaspes rescues his stricken son from death.
claims.statement_id: Dalam kutipan Nonnus, Hydaspes menyelamatkan putranya dari kematian.
claims.quote:
but Hydaspes rescued his
        stricken son from death.

claims.statement: Jatasura is a rakshasa in the Mahabharata killed by Bhima.
claims.statement_id: Jatasura adalah raksasa dalam Mahabharata yang dibunuh Bhima.
claims.quote: is a rakshasa in the Hindu epic Mahabharata. ... He is slain by Bhima.

claims.statement: He poses as a Brahmin to gain the Pandavas' trust.
claims.statement_id: Ia menyamar sebagai brahmana untuk mendapatkan kepercayaan Pandawa.
claims.quote: According to the Mahabharata, Jatasura appeared in the guise of a Brahmin to the Pandavas. His goal was to gain their confidence

claims.statement: When Bhima is away he becomes monstrous, seizes weapons, and abducts Yudhishthira, Sahadeva, Nakula, and Draupadi.
claims.statement_id: Saat Bhima pergi, ia mengambil wujud monster serta merampas senjata dan menculik Yudhishthira, Sahadeva, Nakula, dan Draupadi.
claims.quote: One day, when Bhima was away, Jatasura assumed a monstrous form. He seized the weapons and also abducted Yudhishthira, Sahadeva, Nakula, and Draupadi.

claims.statement: Sahadeva escapes and seeks Bhima's help.
claims.statement_id: Sahadeva lolos dan mencari bantuan Bhima.
claims.quote: Sahadeva managed to escape from his grasp, and rushed to seek the aid of Bhima.

claims.statement: Yudhishthira confuses him with moral accusations.
claims.statement_id: Yudhishthira membingungkannya dengan tuduhan moral.
claims.quote: Yudhishthira confused their captor by showering him with moral accusations, observing Jatasura's lack of intelligence.

claims.statement: He fights Bhima with huge trees, rocks, and hands before being defeated.
claims.statement_id: Ia melawan Bhima menggunakan pohon besar, batu, dan tangan sebelum dikalahkan.
claims.quote: The Pandava and the rakshasa fought with gigantic trees, large rocks, along with their arms. ... In the end, Bhima was able to inflict a death blow on his opponent's neck.

claims.statement: In this abridged Mahabharata, the rakshasa disguised himself as a brahmana and secretly stayed with the Pandavas, claiming to be a high-class brahmana; his real desire was to steal their bows, quivers and other possessions.
claims.statement_id: Dalam ringkasan Mahabharata ini, raksasa itu menyamar sebagai brahmana dan diam-diam tinggal bersama para Pandawa dengan mengaku brahmana berkedudukan tinggi; keinginannya yang sebenarnya adalah mencuri busur, tabung panah, dan harta milik mereka.
claims.quote: That Rakshasa, who had been disguised as a brahmana, had secretly remained in the company of the Pandavas, alleging that he was a high class brahmana. His real desire was to steal the bows, quivers and other possessions of the Pandavas.

claims.statement: The name of this wicked demon was Jatasura.
claims.statement_id: Raksasa jahat itu bernama Jatasura.
claims.quote: The name of this wicked demon was Jatasura.

claims.statement: Sahadeva broke free of the demon's grip and forcefully took the sword named Kausika from his grasp.
claims.statement_id: Sahadeva melepaskan diri dari cengkeraman sang iblis dan dengan kuat merebut pedang bernama Kausika dari genggamannya.
claims.quote: However, Sahadeva broke away from the demon's grip and forcefully took the sword named Kausika from his grasp.

claims.statement: In the fight the two combatants repeatedly uprooted trees and struck each other, shouting, then picked up rocks and flung them at each other.
claims.statement_id: Dalam pertarungan itu, kedua petarung berulang kali mencabut pohon dan saling memukul sambil berteriak, lalu mengambil batu dan saling melemparkannya.
claims.quote: Repeatedly uprooting trees, they hit each other, shouting and roaring like two masses of clouds. ... those two warriors picked up rocks and flung them at each other.

claims.statement: Bhima repeatedly struck the rakshasa's neck and severed his head from his body.
claims.statement_id: Bhima berulang kali memukul leher sang raksasa dan memisahkan kepalanya dari tubuhnya.
claims.quote: Striking the Rakshasa's neck repeatedly, Bhima severed his head from his body.

claims.statement: Lakhey is a Nepalese folklore demon with a fierce face, fangs, and a red, white, or black mane.
claims.statement_id: Lakhey adalah iblis cerita rakyat Nepal berwajah ganas, bertaring, dan bersurai merah, putih, atau hitam.
claims.quote: is a demon in Nepalese folklore. He is depicted with a ferocious face, protruding fangs and a mane of red, white or black hair.

claims.statement: The tradition is prominent in Newar culture of Nepal Mandala.
claims.statement_id: Tradisinya menonjol dalam budaya Newar Nepal Mandala.
claims.quote: Lakhes figure prominently in the traditional Newar culture of Nepal Mandala.

claims.statement: They are said to dwell in forests before becoming protectors of townspeople.
claims.statement_id: Mereka dikisahkan tinggal di hutan sebelum menjadi pelindung warga kota.
claims.quote: Lakhes are said to be demons who used to live in the forests and later became protectors to the townspeople.

claims.statement: A female Lakhey is called Lasin.
claims.statement_id: Lakhey perempuan disebut Lasin.
claims.quote: A female Lakhe is known as Lasin

claims.statement: Kathmandu's Majipa Lakhey appears during Yenya or Indra Jatra and is worshipped as a deity.
claims.statement_id: Majipa Lakhey Kathmandu muncul saat Yenya atau Indra Jatra dan dipuja sebagai dewa.
claims.quote: The most famous Lakhe is Majipa Lakhey of Kathmandu who appears during the Yenya (Indra Jatra) festival in September. He is worshipped as a deity. City dwellers offer food and ritual items to him as he moves through the city accompanied by his musical band giving dance performances.

claims.statement: Nepal Tourism Board records masked Lakhay dancers taking to the streets almost nightly with loud drums during Indra Jatra.
claims.statement_id: Nepal Tourism Board mencatat penari bertopeng Lakhay turun ke jalan hampir tiap malam diiringi genderang keras dalam Indra Jatra.
claims.quote: Masked dancers known as Lakhay take to the streets almost every evening accompanied by loud drums.

claims.statement: Taoroinai is a snake like dragon in Meitei mythology and Manipur's Sanamahism dwelling in the land of the Moon.
claims.statement_id: Taoroinai adalah naga menyerupai ular dalam mitologi Meitei dan Sanamahism Manipur yang tinggal di negeri Bulan.
claims.quote: is a snake-like dragon in Meitei mythology and Sanamahism, the indigenous religion of Manipur. It lived in the land of the Moon.

claims.statement: The Shakok Lamlen says Kangla was built over his navel.
claims.statement_id: Shakok Lamlen menyebut Kangla dibangun di atas pusarnya.
claims.quote: According to the Shakok Lamlen, the Kangla was constructed over the navel of Taoroinai.

claims.statement: The Sanggai Phammang recounts him carrying Atiya's image to earth in his mouth, the image later being born as a divine boy.
claims.statement_id: Sanggai Phammang menuturkan ia membawa citra Atiya ke bumi dalam mulut, kemudian citra itu lahir sebagai anak ilahi.
claims.quote: According to the Sanggai Phammang, Taoroinai lived on the Moon. He was ordered by the God Atiya (Atingkok) to carry His image to the Earth. He swallowed the image of the God in his mouth and brought it down. He lived inside the Earth. The God's image was later born as a divine boy.

claims.statement: The Leithak Leikharol and Krathok Lamlen recount a Tupu disguise to bring Atiya's cloud egg, later becoming Pakhangba.
claims.statement_id: Leithak Leikharol dan Krathok Lamlen menuturkan penyamaran sebagai Tupu untuk membawa telur awan Atiya yang kemudian menjadi Pakhangba.
claims.quote: According to the Leithak Leikharol and the Krathok Lamlen, Taoroinai went to the heavens disguises as Tupu (officer in charge) and brought down the divine cloud egg (nonglum) of Atiya. He gave the egg to a polyandrous person. Later, the egg became Pakhangba.

claims.statement: The Leimaren Naoyom recounts him giving an embryonic egg to Leimarel Sidabi, who later bears Pakhangba.
claims.statement_id: Leimaren Naoyom menuturkan ia memberikan telur embrio kepada Leimarel Sidabi yang kemudian melahirkan Pakhangba.
claims.quote: According to the Leimaren Naoyom, Taoroinai gave an embryonic egg to Leimarel Sidabi, a solar goddess (or a celestial goddess). Later, goddess Leimaren (alias Yaibirok) gave birth to Pakhangba.

claims.statement: The Anoirol recounts him teaching his daughter Toibi Tanka Nubi to dance.
claims.statement_id: Anoirol menuturkan ia mengajari putrinya Toibi Tanka Nubi menari.
claims.quote: According to the Anoirol, Lady Toibi Tanka Nubi (Tankha Chanu) danced with her father, Taoroinai. She learned how to dance from Taoroinai step by step and movement by movement.

claims.statement: A journal article on nature worship says Panthoibi, the consort of Nongpok Ningthou, is the daughter of Taoroinai and Lainamung Namungba, and describes her as a great goddess of mankind.
claims.statement_id: Sebuah artikel jurnal tentang pemujaan alam menyebut Panthoibi, permaisuri Nongpok Ningthou, sebagai putri Taoroinai dan Lainamung Namungba, dan menggambarkannya sebagai dewi besar umat manusia.
claims.quote: Nongpok Ningthou and his divine consort Panthoibi are taken to be indispensable. The Meiteis generally worship them as NongpokPanthoibi. She is the daughter of Taoroinai and Lainamung Namungba, is described as a great goddess of mankind

claims.statement: Tarkshya is a Rigvedic being described as a horse with the epithet arishta nemi.
claims.statement_id: Tarkshya adalah makhluk Rigveda yang digambarkan sebagai kuda dengan sebutan arishta-nemi.
claims.quote: is the name of a mythical being in the Rigveda, described as a horse with the epithet áriṣṭa-nemi

claims.statement: An alternative interpretation regards him as a bird.
claims.statement_id: Tafsir alternatif menganggapnya burung.
claims.quote: but alternatively taken to be a bird (RV 5.51)

claims.statement: The Mahabharata and Harivamsha later identify him with Garuda.
claims.statement_id: Mahabharata dan Harivamsha kemudian menyamakannya dengan Garuda.
claims.quote: later identified with Garuda (Mahabharata, Harivamsha)

claims.statement: The Bhagavata Purana also associates the name with Garuda's father.
claims.statement_id: Bhagavata Purana juga mengaitkan nama itu dengan ayah Garuda.
claims.quote: or Garuda's father (Bhagavata Purana 6.6.2, 21)

claims.statement: The Mahabharata counts him among Kashyapa's offspring.
claims.statement_id: Mahabharata memasukkannya di antara keturunan Kashyapa.
claims.quote: counted among the offspring of Kashyapa in Mahabharata 1.2548, 4830 and 12468.

claims.statement: The epithet arishta nemi is explained as with intact wheel rims.
claims.statement_id: Sebutan arishta-nemi diterangkan berarti dengan pinggir roda yang utuh.
claims.quote: with the epithet áriṣṭa-nemi "with intact wheel-rims"

claims.statement: In this translated Rigveda hymn, Tarkshya is invoked for welfare and described as mighty, commissioned by the gods, victorious, the outstripper of chariots, of irresistible car, the overthrower of hosts, and swift.
claims.statement_id: Dalam terjemahan himne Rigveda ini, Tarkshya diseru demi kesejahteraan dan disifati perkasa, ditugaskan para dewa, pemenang, pelampaui kereta, berkereta tak terkalahkan, penakluk pasukan, dan cepat.
claims.quote: Let us invoke here for our welfare that Tārkṣya, who is mighty, the commissioned of the gods, thevictorious, the outstripper of chariots, of irresistible car, the overthrower of hosts, the swift.

claims.statement: The commentary accompanying the hymn equates Tarkshya with suparna, the son of Trksa, commissioned by the gods to bring the Soma from heaven.
claims.statement_id: Komentar yang menyertai himne itu menyamakan Tarkshya dengan suparna, putra Trksa, yang ditugaskan para dewa membawa Soma dari surga.
claims.quote: Tārk.sya: i.e.,suparṇa, the son of Tṛkṣa, commissioned by the gods to bring the Soma from heaven

claims.statement: In another Rigveda verse, Tarkshya, with unblemished weapons, is asked to guard the welfare of those invoking him.
claims.statement_id: Dalam himne Rigveda lain, Tarkshya yang bersenjata tanpa cela dimohon menjaga kesejahteraan para penyeru.
claims.quote: may Tārkṣya, with unblemished weapons, guard our welfare.

claims.statement: The commentary on this verse says Tarkshya, son of Trksa, is Garuda, and explains Aristanemi as he who has unharmed or irresistible weapons (nemi being the circumference of a wheel).
claims.statement_id: Komentar pada himne ini menyebut Tarkshya, putra Trksa, adalah Garuda, dan menafsirkan Aristanemi sebagai ia yang memiliki senjata tak rusak atau tak terkalahkan (nemi berarti lingkar roda).
claims.quote: Tārkṣya, son of Tṛkṣa is Garuḍa. He is Ariṣṭanemi, he who has unharmed or irresistible (aṛṣṭa) weapons (nemi, circumerference of a wheel).

claims.statement: The Twelve Heavenly Generals are protective deities or yakshas of Bhaisajyaguru, the healing Buddha, in East Asian Buddhism.
claims.statement_id: Dua Belas Jenderal Langit adalah dewa pelindung atau yaksha Bhaisajyaguru, Buddha penyembuhan, dalam Buddha Asia Timur.
claims.quote: In East Asian Buddhism, the Twelve Heavenly Generals or Twelve Divine Generals are the protective deities, or yaksha, of Bhaisajyaguru, the buddha of healing.

claims.statement: They are introduced in the Medicine Buddha Sutra.
claims.statement_id: Mereka diperkenalkan dalam Medicine Buddha Sutra.
claims.quote: They are introduced in the Medicine Buddha Sutra

claims.statement: Their precise names can differ by tradition.
claims.statement_id: Nama tepat mereka dapat berbeda menurut tradisi.
claims.quote: The precise names of the generals seem to vary depending on tradition. Those listed below are from an available Sanskrit transcription of the Bhaiṣajyaguruvaiḍūryaprabhārāja Sūtra:

claims.statement: Their zodiac and honji correspondences also vary by text and region.
claims.statement_id: Pemetaan zodiak dan honji juga bervariasi menurut teks dan daerah.
claims.quote: While the Honji and zodiac correspondences listed above are the standard in Japanese sources, there is variation among texts and regional traditions.

claims.statement: In Japanese tradition they guard twelve times, months, or directions corresponding to the healing Buddha's twelve vows.
claims.statement_id: Dalam tradisi Jepang mereka menjaga dua belas waktu, bulan, atau arah sesuai dua belas ikrar Buddha penyembuhan.
claims.quote: 十二神将は、薬師如来の十二の大願に応じて、それぞれが昼夜の十二の時、十二の月、または十二の方角を守るという。そのため中国や日本では十二支が配当された。また、十二神将にはそれぞれ本地（化身前の本来の姿）の如来・菩薩・明王がある。

claims.statement: Each general leads seven thousand yakshas, totaling eighty four thousand.
claims.statement_id: Setiap jenderal memimpin tujuh ribu yaksha, total delapan puluh empat ribu.
claims.quote: 各神将がそれぞれ7千、総計8万4千の眷属夜叉を率い、それは人間の持つ煩悩の数に対応しているという。

claims.statement: Uchek Langmeitong is a Meitei tale of Hayainu becoming a hornbill because of her stepmother's mistreatment.
claims.statement_id: Uchek Langmeitong adalah kisah Meitei tentang Hayainu yang menjadi rangkong karena perlakuan buruk ibu tirinya.
claims.quote: is a Meitei folktale of Ancient Kangleipak (early Manipur). It is the story of a girl named "Hayainu" ... who turned herself into a Langmeitong (Meitei for 'hornbill bird') as she was unable to suffer the ill treatments of her cruel stepmother.

claims.statement: Hayainu is also called Nongdam Atombi.
claims.statement_id: Hayainu juga disebut Nongdam Atombi.
claims.quote: a girl named "Hayainu" (alias Nongdam Atombi)

claims.statement: Her father leaves to earn money, leaving her with a stepmother who forces her to work and beats her.
claims.statement_id: Ayahnya pergi mencari penghasilan dan meninggalkannya bersama ibu tiri yang memaksanya bekerja serta memukulinya.
claims.quote: Hayainu's father moved across the country to earn more money for his family. ... her stepmother asked her to do all the household works. ... she was hated and would be beaten up by her cruel stepmother every day.

claims.statement: Her dead mother appears in a dream and suggests collecting hornbill feathers.
claims.statement_id: Ibunya yang sudah meninggal muncul dalam mimpi dan menyarankan mengumpulkan bulu rangkong.
claims.quote: Once in Hayainu's dream, her real mother told her to go to the world of the Langmeidongs (Hornbills). ... to give her some of their feathers, collect and stitch them to her body and flew away.

claims.statement: She stitches feathers into cloth wrapped around her, and a flock of hornbills lifts her into flight.
claims.statement_id: Ia menjahit bulu pada kain yang membalut dirinya, kemudian kawanan rangkong mengangkatnya terbang.
claims.quote: Then, she sewed the feathers into the wrapped clothes. ... The birds picked her up and she flew away with them.

claims.statement: Sharma's Funga Wari Singbul version names the girl Nongdangnu, becoming a bird and waiting for her father in a tree.
claims.statement_id: Versi Funga Wari Singbul Sharma menyebut gadis Nongdangnu yang berubah menjadi burung dan menunggu ayahnya di pohon.
claims.quote: The next day Nongdangnu turned as a bird sat on the branched of a tree waiting for her father's arrival.

claims.statement: Aana Marutha is a mythological figure of Kerala, India.
claims.statement_id: Aana Marutha adalah figur mitos Kerala, India.
claims.quote: is a mythological figure popular in the Indian state of Kerala.

claims.statement: The article depicts her as a bloodsucking evil spirit.
claims.statement_id: Artikel menggambarkannya sebagai roh jahat pengisap darah.
claims.quote: Aana Marutha is often depicted as a bloodsucking evil spirit.

claims.statement: She is said to seduce solitary people before attacking and draining their blood.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan menggoda orang yang sendirian sebelum menyerang dan menguras darah mereka.
claims.quote: She seduces lonely people before attacking them and draining their blood.

claims.statement: She is described with fangs and bloodshot eyes.
claims.statement_id: Ia digambarkan bertaring dan bermata merah.
claims.quote: Aana Marutha is described as having fangs and bloodshot eyes.

claims.statement: She is said to leave backwards footprints.
claims.statement_id: Ia dikatakan meninggalkan jejak kaki terbalik.
claims.quote: She is said to leave backwards footprints.

claims.statement: The 2021 short film Kandittund! depicts Aana Marutha as a one and a half foot elephant like creature with an iron ankle chain.
claims.statement_id: Film pendek Kandittund! tahun 2021 menggambarkan Aana Marutha sebagai makhluk mirip gajah setinggi satu setengah kaki dengan rantai besi di pergelangan kaki.
claims.quote: The 2021 short film Kandittund! (Seen It!) from Studio Eeksaurus describes Aana Marutha as a one-and-a-half foot tall elephant-like creature with an iron chain around its ankle.

claims.statement: The film report describes Panicker's version as an elephant like creature one and a half feet tall.
claims.statement_id: Liputan film menerangkan versi kisah Panicker yang menyerupai gajah setinggi satu setengah kaki.
claims.quote: Aana marutha is a peculiar one-and-a-half-foot elephant-like creature,
